title: Clock and Atlas
premise: In the winter after a war nobody will name honestly, Oscar Amberdale keeps a hidden ledger of the soldiers, civilians, and deserters the official reports erase. When the season's last bridge closes and a dying colonel entrusts her with documents proving a sanctioned massacre, Oscar becomes the only living custodian of the truth. Trapped in the river town as victors' historians arrive to fix the record forever, she must decide which names to protect, which to expose, and what her own silence has cost. The novel ends as the ice breaks: Oscar testifies, the ledger enters the record under every name it holds, and she finally writes her own true name on the first page.
about_author: Petra Iversen is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing war correspondence in municipal collections across northern Europe. She writes about the people history files under 'miscellaneous.'

chapters.title: The Ledger Under the Floorboard
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Twelve years after the war, she tends the convalescent ward of a river garrison hospital and adds a new name to her hidden ledger: a private the officers recorded as 'unaccounted.' The emotional beat is quiet dread — the habit of secrecy has become her whole character.

chapters.title: Ice Forming at the Pilings
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The town buzzes with news: the bridge closes for the season within the week, cutting the garrison off until spring. Oscar realizes her window to send the ledger out is closing. The beat is urgency disguised as routine.

chapters.title: The Colonel's Cough
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Colonel Vasseur, a decorated officer she has quietly despised for twelve years, is admitted with pneumonia and recognizes her from the field hospital. The beat is the collision of two people who each know what the other did to survive.

chapters.title: What Vasseur Kept
chapters.summary: Vasseur's POV. Delirious, the colonel confesses to ordering the withdrawal that stranded the civilians at Kolvik Bridge, then gives Oscar a locked dispatch case: orders, rosters, photographs. The beat is a guilty man buying absolution with someone else's burden.

chapters.title: The Bridge Closes
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The last cart crosses; the bridge is chained and posted. Oscar stands on the bank with the dispatch case hidden in her coat and understands she is trapped with her evidence and her enemies. The beat is the door shutting.

chapters.title: The Historians Arrive
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Two victors' historians arrive by sledge to compile the official campaign record, staying at the garrison. One, a young archivist named Ilse, seems genuinely curious. The beat is hope arriving wearing the enemy's uniform.

chapters.title: Names the Reports Forgot
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse interviews Oscar as a 'material witness' and is puzzled by small discrepancies in the official rosters. Oscar gives her truth in fragments, testing her. The beat is two careful women circling each other with the truth between them like a lit lamp.

chapters.title: The Widow from Kolvik
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Marta, a Kolvik survivor now working in the laundry, recognizes the dispatch case's seal. Her fury forces Oscar to admit the ledger exists. The beat is betrayal turning into an alliance neither woman trusts.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Flashback, Oscar's POV. The field hospital at Kolvik: the order to abandon the civilians, the officer who made Oscar burn the first list, the name she saved by lying. The beat is the origin of her silence and her ledger.

chapters.title: A Search of the Ward
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The garrison commandant, warned that 'documents are circulating,' orders the hospital searched. Oscar hides the case inside a dead man's belongings. The beat is terror in the mundane machinery of bureaucracy.

chapters.title: Ilse's Doubt
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse discovers her senior historian is editing testimony to flatter a living general. She copies a suppressed page and, on instinct, shows it to no one — yet. The beat is the moment an institution's employee becomes a person.

chapters.title: The Colonel Dies
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Vasseur dies at dawn, whispering the Kolvik numbers to a room of orderlies. Officially he died of pneumonia, a hero. The beat is grief for a man she hated, and the horror of watching a lie being born in real time.

chapters.title: The Hero's Funeral
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The garrison buries Vasseur with honors; the commandant's eulogy rewrites Kolvik as a 'tragic necessity.' Marta spits in the snow; Oscar holds her arm. The beat is public memory being manufactured before their eyes.

chapters.title: A Bargain in the Dispensary
chapters.summary: Oscar and Ilse's POV, alternating. Oscar shows Ilse one page of the ledger; Ilse reveals the historians' mandate expires when the ice breaks — after that, the record is sealed. The beat is trust extended as a calculated gamble.

chapters.title: The Commandant's Offer
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The commandant privately offers Oscar a transfer, a pension, and silence — he knows what she carries. He also reveals he was at Kolvik. The beat is temptation priced in survival, the novel's theme made flesh.

chapters.title: What Marta Asks For
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. Marta demands her husband's name in the record, even if exposure endangers them all; Oscar resists, wanting to protect her people. The beat is the clash between safety and dignity, between the survivor's silence and the dead's claim.

chapters.title: The Copy
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse secretly types a duplicate testimony; Oscar and Marta copy the ledger by lamplight, page by page, three nights running. The beat is exhausted, sacred work — memory made physical again.

chapters.title: Betrayal
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. An orderly sells them out; the dispatch case is seized and the commandant moves to arrest Oscar before the ice breaks. Ilse burns her own notes to protect Oscar and loses her position. The beat is everything lost at once — and the plan forced into the open.

chapters.title: Before the Historians
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, climax. At the public closing session, Oscar stands uninvited and reads the Kolvik names aloud from memory — all of them — while Marta and the ward staff stand in witness. The commandant cannot stop her without confirming her. The beat is the silence of twelve years breaking like the river.

chapters.title: The Ice Breaks
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. The river cracks and groans; the bridge reopens. Ilse enters the full testimony and the ledger into the record over her superior's objection, then resigns. The beat is a small bureaucratic act that will outlast every general.

chapters.title: The First Page
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The commandant is quietly retired rather than tried — the price of survival persists — but the names stand. Oscar walks the repaired bridge, carrying Marta's flowers to the far bank. The beat is imperfect justice, honestly rendered.

chapters.title: Oscar Amberdale, Witness
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. In spring, Oscar writes her own name, rank, and full account on the ledger's first page and donates it to Ilse's archive, no longer hidden under a floorboard. The final beat: identity reclaimed — she was never just a keeper of other people's names.
